Agreeing in principle to set up a subcommittee on the health of older persons and social welfare
se: The committee considered setting up a subcommittee, as the Subcommittee to Follow Progress on the Primary Health Care System has finished its work and reported to the Senate. A vice-chair of the committee proposed a subcommittee to study all aspects of older persons and people with dependency, continuing from the previous meeting on the care of older persons and the safety of service users. An adviser to the committee presented a study framework, for example linking the health system, long-term care and social protection with older persons and their families at the centre, linking data between agencies safely under the personal data protection law, reviewing the NHSO's long-term care budget allocation, and studying local models such as in Chiang Mai, Phuket and Songkhla, over about 3 months (March–May 2027). Committee members observed, for example, that family institutions should be strengthened, financial literacy of older persons promoted, and people prepared from working age. The committee agreed in principle to set up a subcommittee on developing the public health system, the health of older persons and social welfare, and agreed to hold part 5 of the forum “The Facts on the Gold Card Bill | What Does the Committee Say?” on Wednesday 9 December 2026.
it: Setting up a subcommittee on developing the public health system, the health of older persons and social welfare (agreed in principle)

Developing care for older persons and people with dependency, and protecting the safety of service users
se: Meeting on Tuesday 10 November 2026, according to the meeting notice. The agenda was a study of developing care for older persons, people with dependency and people who need special care, including protecting the rights and safety of service users, continuing from the news about a care centre for older persons in Kanchanaburi and the admission of people with drug addiction or psychiatric disorders into care businesses for older persons. Standards of care for older persons and dependent patients in care facilities
se: Meeting on Tuesday 3 November 2026, according to the meeting notice. The agenda was a study, following news about a care centre for older persons and dependent patients in Kanchanaburi, of the standards and safety of care facilities, and of setting criteria and standards for the care of older persons and people with dependency, including people with drug addiction or psychiatric disorders. (The Senate published the meeting summary as an image file. Please read the details in the original documents below.)
it: Standards and safety in the care of older persons and dependent patients in facilities, and criteria for care

Community hospital finances, and standards for care centres for older persons
se: The committee heard the chair of the Association of Community Hospital Directors of Thailand, who said community hospitals' income has grown but spending has grown faster, especially for small hospitals serving few people, and budget allocation and service payments still do not match costs. The committee proposed, for example, reviewing allocation and payment criteria to match the real costs and workload of hospitals at each level, a mechanism to support cash flow together with recovery plans, speeding up payments and outstanding debts, and sharing resources at province and health region level. It also took up a news report about a care centre for older persons and dependent patients in Kanchanaburi to consider standards and safety of care.
it: Finances of community hospitals (Association of Community Hospital Directors of Thailand)

Hospital finances (continued): hearing the association of regional and general hospitals and hospitals in the field
se: The committee continued to study the finances of hospitals under the Office of the Permanent Secretary for Public Health. The chair of the association of regional and general hospitals reported 93 hospitals at financial risk level 7 (mostly community hospitals) and 540 service units, or about 59 percent, with negative maintenance funds. The director of a network hospital in Chiang Mai described a shortage of cash at the end of fiscal year 2026, which affected buying medicines and medical supplies, because of several outstanding debts, including treatment costs for migrant workers. The committee considered the effects on buying medicines and supplies and on staff management, and possible solutions.
it: Finances of hospitals under the Office of the Permanent Secretary for Public Health: income, spending, maintenance funds and debts
